title: Slow startup from too many startup apps
symptom: PC takes several minutes to become usable after sign-in
user_description: It takes forever to get going in the morning. I sign in and then wait five minutes before I can open anything.

options.text: Disable every startup item, including security software
options.why: Switching off security software leaves the PC unprotected. Only non-essential items should be disabled.
Drastic and usually unnecessary. Startup programs are a far likelier cause than Windows itself.

options.text: Open the Startup tab in Task Manager, sort by impact, and disable non-essential programs after asking which ones she really needs
options.why: Many programs start automatically and compete for resources at sign-in. Task Manager shows which have the highest startup impact, and asking the user avoids disabling something she needs.

options.text: Delete the startup programs' folders from Program Files
options.why: Destructive. It breaks the programs instead of just stopping them from starting automatically.

hints: What happens in the minutes after someone signs in?
Where in Windows can you see what starts automatically?
Which items should you never switch off?
real_world_tip: Look for chat apps, updaters and sync tools. They are the usual heavy startup items and are safe to start manually.
